text:
The Sharks have lost seven of eight, and Macklin Celebrini is being asked to carry all of it. He played a career-high 28:05 in Dallas on Saturday, the second night of a back-to-back, with nobody else on the team above 23:44 (Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest). Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov are on injured reserve, Michael Misa has moved up to Celebrini's wing, and the five-game skid is not bad luck: 40% of the expected goals, outscored 22-8. Celebrini is one point from 200 for his career. Will Smith is one goal from 50 and Mason Marchment one from 100.

What has hurt San Jose most is the penalty kill. It allows 1.06 expected goals a game, the most of any team playing tonight, and gave up five goals in the last two. That matters, because the Islanders take 4.7 penalties a game, also the most of anyone on tonight's slate.

New York flies west winless in three and banged up. Ryan Pulock, Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie are out, and the lineup keeps reshuffling around it: Simon Holmstrom has jumped to 20:44 a night and onto the first power-play unit. He is our Sleeper for a point at 52%, well above his season pace. The last game was the kind that lingers. The Islanders led the Devils 4-2, lost 5-4 in overtime on a Jack Hughes winner, and Matthew Schaefer, the 2025 first overall pick, ended up trading punches with Luke Hughes. Ilya Sorokin (+6.1 goals saved above expected) is the reason they are still at 17 points and a 21% playoff chance.

Yaroslav Askarov has been good too, +4.4 this season after a rough year. Our numbers favour the Islanders, 3.35 expected goals to 3.08, with Ivar Stenberg, a third-liner getting to dangerous ice, as the Sharks' Sleeper.
headline: Celebrini's minutes, San Jose's penalty kill

hunch.text: The slate's most penalized team visits the leakiest penalty kill on the slate. Even with Sorokin and Askarov in net, our gut says this one goes over.
